en: Chol'aruk the Ravener
Bring the head of Chol'aruk to Gur'ak in the Barrens.

You there, $c. I need your aid. There are rumors of a beast that makes its lair deep in a cave at Thorn Hill, northeast of here. The Razormane call it Chol'aruk or "The Ravener". It's supposedly five times the size of a normal quilboar with a thirst for blood that can never be sated.

Most don't believe the tales. But I do--because I've fought its like before.

Seek out its lair and slay Chol'aruk. Bring me its head. I warn you though--prepare well and do not go alone.

Blood and thunder, $c.

It took the strength of six skilled fighters to defeat one of these creatures, and it still managed to fell four of us before we could put it down.

If these monstrous beasts were to appear in greater numbers, the damage that the qullboar could inflict upon the land could be catastrophic.

Impressive, $c. None will doubt my tales when I return to Orgrimmar with this grim proof of the existence of these abominations. Rest assured this glory is yours however, and I will speak loudly of your deeds.

Lok-tar!
Chol'aruk the Ravener
Bring Chol'aruk's Head to Bainham in the Barrens.

There are rumors of a colossal abomination that makes its lair at a cave to the northwest of here, on the plateau known as Thorn Hill. The Razormane call it Chol'aruk or "The Ravener" and those that have seen it say it's so massive that it can swallow an orc whole.

Few believe such tales, but I do... because I've fought one like it myself. On the honor of those I lost to these things, this beast must die.

Gather strong allies and find the lair of Chol'aruk. Kill the abomination and bring me its head.
Tip the Scales - Keefer's Angelfish
Tip the Scales - Brownell's Blue Striped Racer
Tip the Scales - Dezian Queenfish
Philmor's Favor
Bring the Gatehouse Shipment to the stockroom entrance located in Trias' Cheese shop in the Trade District.

Every day this week we've been short dockhands.

Care to ease the stress on our cargo schedule?

Take this package to the stockroom entrance of the Gatehouse. You'll find it inside Trias' Cheese shop on the second floor. The mistress, Elaine, will be quite familiar with the deliveries. The Gatehouse often has shipments arriving with more discretion to allow for ceremonial surprises on behalf of the guard's officers.
You looking to fill a crate with our finest aged wheels?
Oh, dear. You think we want to carry that up the stairs ourselves? Keeping the valuables intact is your responsibility up until the point you drop it off.
Gatehouse Goods
Carry the Gatehouse Shipment up the stairs in Trias' shop and leave it outside the door.

Yes, it's only a flight of stairs, but if it's such a small ask, it should be no problem for you to finish the delivery yourself! 

Trias' Cheese isn't part of the Gatehouse or their stocking inventory, but our buildings share a floor.

Place the crate outside their stockroom door--the guard will send someone for a regular pickup. They will see the package arrival and carry it inside as they return to post.
You should at least try some of this aged cheddar. You can't stop eating it.

Yep. There's a reason that hinge opens inwards towards them, so they don't get the door blocked by people leaving stuff anywhere they please.

Consider us professionally acquainted, $c. 

We respect your business, and expect you to respect ours.
Bloodtalon Matriarch
Bring Eggs of the Bloodtalon Matriarch to Xar'Ti in Sen'jin Village.

All of the raptors you see before you are ones I have trained myself. They come from all over Kalimdor, but some of the finest come from the Bloodtalon raptors on the isles off our coast.

One raptor amongst them, the Bloodtalon Matriarch, is particularly savage and has killed many from our village and has become too dangerous to leave at our borders. If you can strike her down, return with her eggs so that we can raise the hatchlings as allies instead of enemies.

The Bloodtalon are known for their cunning and swiftness, and make fine companions when raised from egg to adult.

Unfortunately adult raptors are very difficult to train, and I have tried to capture the Matriarch on more than one occasion. But she had become too dangerous of late.

Still I hope to preserve her legacy by raising her children as companions here in Sen'Jin.
Thank you, $N. I am happy we will be able to preserve her bloodline and raise them to be our allies. You have done a great service for our tribe.
Forgotten Loa Idols
Collect $1oa Forgotten Loa Idols from the Echo Isles. Bring them to Master Gadrin in Sen'jin Village.

When we fled the isles that Zalazane and his ilk now inhabit, we left behind many precious idols that help us commune with spirits we worship: our loa. They are of grave importance to our tribe.

The followers of Zalazane show no reverence for our loa and have scattered these idols across the largest of the isles.

This is an action that will not go unnoticed if we are not able to collect these idols, and offending a loa is a grave matter.

Go, find as many loa idols as you can and return them to me.
Have you found our loa idols, $N? We must begin our rituals again soon.

You have done a great deed for our tribe today.

Unlike some tribes, our kinship with our loa is one of reverence and respect, and we owe them much.

I would not want the Darkspear to fall out of favor with them.
Reading Room
Bring the wrapped reading material to the Stormwind library.

Are you here to discuss the deeper meanings of our storied legends? No?

Well, after you're done looking around, can you carry this to the library for me? We're exchanging some of our less popular bodies of work for some more modern writing. I have a list of tomes I'm quite sure the librarian will be able to procure for us within our existing arrangement.

Complimentary club refreshments on us, if you help us out.
Fang of Githyiss
Deliver the Fang of Githyiss to someone interested in the study of spiders in Aldrassil.
A fresh specimen from a beast of this size is quite a find. Perhaps someone in Aldrassil familiar with the study of spiders would be interested in the fang.

My, my. How I do love surprises, $N.

This specimen will surely help further my studies.
Shelf Picked
Find each of the reading materials located somewhere in the library and then return to Roy Lewells in Stormwind's Park.

I've checked our inventory and all of the selections Mr. Lewells has listed are currently available.

You will, however, need to procure them off the shelves yourself. Part of our librarian duty is vigilance, and for that, I will resume supervisory bookkeeping.

Returning with the material to Roy on his behalf will not mark yourself accountable for their return; as with his note you're serving as the book club's official courier. Their establishment shall carry that burden.

Good day, $n.
Yelmak's Medley
Take some cuttings from the Cattails and Speargrass growing around the water flows in the Valley of Honor and return to Kor'geld in Yelmak's Alchemy and Potions.

Yelmak doesn't want his apprentice breaking anything. Well, anything more than he already has.

He told me the young mixer in training has too much pride to ask for help when he really needs it. Yelmak wants to give him a taste of a particular home-brewed recipe.

Gather a mix of cattail and speargrass cuttings taken from the plants growing around the water in the Valley of Honor. I'd get them myself, but if I left the shop, Whuut would surely know we're catering to his mood.
Call of Fire
Bring the Torch of Dormant Flame to Olariaan Swiftburn at the Shrine of Flames in the Gustberry Lowlands.

Even though we are in the realm of Skywall, this is still the elemental plane. The spirits of all four elements speak to us, if we deign to listen. One among us Windshapers is in particular attunement with the element of fire. A shen'dorei by the name of Olariaan Swiftburn.

Bring this to him at the Shrine of Flames in the Gustberry Lowlands. You'll find it tucked away along the edge of the island, west of Valanaar.
Yes, $N? What do you have there?
So you've brought the torch. Yes, young $c, I can teach you to heed the call of fire. It will not be easy, but nothing that we do in this realm is ever easy.
Call of Fire
Slay Skypriest Faladiel in the Gustberry Lowlands and collect Faladiel's Heart.

There is an Al'Aketh Skypriest called Faladiel. He was once a caller of the flame and a stalwart Windshaper. Like so many Al'Aketh, he mortgaged his loyalty for power and his hands are now stained with the blood of his former brothers and sisters.

You will find Skypriest Faladiel at the farm to the northeast past Valanaar, just to the south of the Shrine of Akir. Kill the betrayer. Bring me his heart. It is a gruesome task, but it is needed for the ritual we are to perform.
The heart of a betrayer is a powerful reagent. The flames will eagerly accept such an offering and burn more intensely as it is consumed.

The Windshapers do not forget, and blood is always paid with blood. It pleases me that you were able to deliver this final, painful reminder of our creed to this traitor.

This heart will not be all that feeds the flames today, however. There is one other task that needs to done.
Call of Fire
Find the home of Kuramaa in the Shen'dar Highlands, and defeat the spirit in combat. Bring Kuramaa's Mask to Olariaan Swiftburn in the Gustberry Lowlands when you are victorious.

The residents of the Shen'dar Highlands speak of an ancient forest sprite called Kuramaa. They say it lives inside of a twisted stump at the summit of a hill near the highlands Anchor Pylon.

Go to the highlands and find this stump. Rap your fist upon the bark and Kuramaa will appear. Best the spirit in combat, and bring me its wooden mask.

Be warned however, this entity will be exceptionally resistant to much of your magic. Only the touch of flame will lay low the spirit.
The spirit of Kuramaa is eternal, and it will manifest again when it is needed. It's mask is a source of great power, and will prove invaluable to the ritual we must complete.
We now have what we need. We will light the eternal flame and commune with the spirits of fire.
Meal Appeal
Visit Borstan's Firepit and tell him Thatog wants you to deliver Migi's lunch to him personally.

My son, Migi, always takes off to play with his friends all day. I tell him to pick up a lunch at Borstan's, but I know he almost never does, because he comes home starving. These kids think their games are more important than their own bodies!

Please, stop at Borstan's Firepit and tell him you're there to deliver Migi's lunch. You can almost certainly find Migi behind Grommash Hold with the rest of his friends.

Duties keep me here during the day and I can't watch over his every meal.

Of course. Migi's parents and I have an arrangement to give Migi a bagged lunch every day, but I can only ensure the boy gets his food if he actually comes in to pick it up.

Sometimes, he doesn't pick up his meal multiple times a week, and I wonder where he gets the energy to stay out and play.
Favorite Food
Bring Migi's Lunch to him behind Grommash Hold.

Now that I know his parents worry about how much he's actually filling that belly, I've got an idea. 

They made me promise not to pack the same meal every day, so Migi grows a taste for more than one thing. Still, whenever the smoker's full and we're making sweetglazed hog belly sandwiches, he always shows up for lunch. We've started crumbling the leftover crispy glazed bits as a topping--something we can add daily. 

Take this to him. Maybe he'll start showing up early and bringing friends!
I think we can win this one...

Borstan's Meats? Is that for one of us?

Oh!

Wow... this smells really good! Yummy.

Thanks for bringing me my lunch. I can tell what Borstan is going to be serving daily when my friends and I walk the road to Grommash Hold, by the smells alone. This tastes like my favorite, the sweetglaze! But it's different. I like the strong flavored crumbs.

If it's going to be this tasty every day, I think we need to stop our game to take our lunch together!
Wrongly Blamed, Justly Corrected
Slay Alliance soldiers encroaching into the Barrens at the border to Dustwallow Marsh, then return to Grunt Logmar at Camp Taurajo.

Traveler, have you plans to head toward Dustwallow Marsh? I have heard mutterings that a few human soldiers have taken a stand at its border and are toppling the landmarks left behind by our tauren pathfinders.

Rumor has it that a favored tavern has burned to the ground, and in typical Alliance fashion, they immediately cast their blame onto the Horde! I cannot know whether there is any truth to their claim, but their incursion onto OUR land must not stand.

Kill first, investigate later!

So the rumors were true! I expected as much, tensions have been rising along the eastern coast for some time. I knew it would only be a matter of time before conflict crept into our territory.

However, I am skeptical that we played a role in the tavern's destruction. Too many Horde civilians rely on that route for trade and travel. Perhaps you could investigate further if you find the time.

In any case, today's deed is a victory for the Horde, and a stern warning to the Alliance!
Parts and Pieces
Collect $1oa Handfuls of Complicated Parts from the upper pirate camp south of Ratchet, then return to Wrenix the Wretched in Ratchet.

Hey, got a sec?

So, apparently, nobody I've sent to deal with the recent pirate problem has come back alive. After five or six attempts I thought, "what if I sent a machine instead?" Turns out, scimitars double as screwdrivers in a pinch, and before I could redirect it home, it was already in pieces and scattered across their camp!

I need those parts back, and since this is a quick little retrieval mission, I'd wager your odds for survival are MUCH higher than the others. Whaddya say?
Not another word out of you until your pockets are jingling with metal!

Whooooa! Nice one, pal! You saved me from another one of Gagsprocket's unbearable lectures on the cost of metal. More importantly, I can jump right into building my next prototype.

Uhhh, I didn't have a reward planned... Do you like boxes?
Call of Fire

Wait for Olariaan to begin the ritual at the Brazier of Offering and follow his instructions.

You must deliver the Eternal Flame to Valanaar before the timer runs out.

Now we will perform the ritual. 

I will place the materials onto the altar and call forth the spirits of flame. If the offering is accepted, they will appear and light the Eternal Flame. You will then hold your torch forth and capture the flame.

Carry the lit torch to Valanaar and place it in the Brazier of Eternal Flames. You must do so quickly, for the flames of the Firelands are quick to dissipate here in Skywall.
You have done well to come this far. You do the Windshapers honor, $N.

It is done. The Eternal Flame burns once again.

Your trial is now complete. I am pleased to present you with your Fire Totem. Use this icon of power well in your travels, $N. 

Just remember, the power of the elemental plane serves those that respect it, and consumes those who do not. This is our way.
Your Package Has Arrived
Deliver Eldrun's misplaced package.
<Several misplaced packages have been left by the mailbox. You note that one of them is marked for delivery from Aerie Peak, to Ironforge, to Eldrun Stormbreaker. It is marked "urgent.">
What's that you've got there?

What! I've been going to the mailbox by the bank every day looking for this package! This city needs to figure out its layout. Not easy to navigate like Aerie Peak!

Let's see what I've got... totem carving tools... spare axe... some kind of goblin device? I didn't order that! Ah, I'll just send it back.

Er, uh... I mean... thank you for bringing all of this to me. Here's a little something for your trouble.
Hate the Hatefury
Defeat a variety of Hatefury satyr at Sargeron in Desolace and then return to Aka'rai in Shadowprey Village.

Ever strike a deal with a satyr, mon?

I have. How could I resist? The promise of power, knowledge far exceeding what any ordinary tome could offer... all alongside an eager and charismatic minion. What more could I ask for?

Bah, of course they would never bend the knee to a mortal. I bargained when I had nothing, only to be cast aside with even less.

Now, I want revenge. Revenge against the Hatefury. Raid their camp to the northeast! Stain the dirt with their foul blood.
Whuut's the Rush
Give Yelmak's Potion to Whuut.

Whuut is a prodigy. That much is true. But he doesn't yet have the experience, wisdom, and time on the stirring rod to know how to respect alchemical processes.

He is exhausting all of the rarest and most exotic reagents we have available without pausing to practice and refine his basic skills.

Give him this potion I've brewed with a quick tonic method. He'll reconsider everything he's doing when he learns how local remedies and careful touch are the first true mastery.
Grund and Gozwin
Find Grund and Gozwin's camp in the hills to the northwest. Recover Gozwin's Mechanic's Log and kill the Snow Leopard Prowler.

Oi, had me back turned gettin' the boar roast ready when I heard me pal Gozwin screamin' fer his life!

Wicked fangs and a blur are all I saw when I turned. Such huge paws! A snow leopard was draggin' its gnomish catch away. I grabbed me shotgun and fired above the beast. It dropped him and sprinted off.

Luckily, it hadn't done more than give ol' Goz some deep scratches.

Head back to camp in the northwestern hills and retrieve Gozwin's Mechanic's Log. Kill that snow leopard too if you see it!
Poor Goz is more concerned for his mecha-walker than himself. Says if anyone gets a hold of that mechanic's log he's greased. Hah! That's why I told him he should just leave his work at home!

Aye, I'm not surprised to hear that snow leopard was makin' a meal of the boar we were fixin' fer roastin'!

Goz will have one less thing to stress about now that you brought back his log book. Maybe now he can focus all his energy on gettin' back on his feet.

Thanks, $N. Take a little something as a token of my appreciation, fer makin' the trek, and fer protectin' the hills.
Wayward Weapons
Collect $1oa Abandoned Training Weapons, then return to Kzan Thornslash in the Den.

With an influx of new recruits like yourself, it's been hard to keep our weapons supplied. Our weaponsmith, Kzan, is running low on training weapons and I'd like to see what kinds of skills you possess to get an idea of what I have to work with. Luckily for you, I have a solution to both.

While you're out there cutting your teeth on boars, salvage six abandoned training weapons. Our failed recruits left them laying on the ground. Once you do, return them to our weaponsmith Kzan behind me in the Den.

Throm'ka, $c. Gorak told me I should be expecting you. It is good to see you in one piece!

Were you able to collect the training weapons I requested?
Thank you for returning these weapons, $N. I will get to work repairing them for the next wave of recruits.
A Simmering Storm
Bring the Dull Stormy Orb to Rezlak near Drygulch Ravine.

<Before you is a strange orb with a dull surface. When picked up a small electrical current seems to vibrate from within. Upon closer inspection, it looks as if a dark mist swirls within and every so often a small electrical spark can be seen.

It is clear the harpy was using it for some purpose. Perhaps Rezlak would be interested in this object?>
Woah, where did you find a neat thing like that? Ya know it reminds me of the other thing my boss Gazlowe always used to tell me...
Stormy Potential
Bring $1oa Charged Thunder Lizard Organs to Rezlak near Drygulch Ravine.

"Rezlack, when an opportunity comes knocking make sure you're ready to seize it." That's another gem Gazlowe taught me and that's exactly what I intend to do.

This orb doesn't seem damaged, it just looks like it's out of juice, but I've the idea to supercharge it back to full strength!

There are a bunch of thunder lizards in a gorge west of here. They have organs that hold a strong electrical charge that would be perfect for this.

Go harvest some and bring them back to me!

It might come as a surprise that with a name like thunder lizard they shoot lightning instead of roaring like thunder.

Well, they do. Shoot lightning, I mean.

Trust me, it's a lesson you only get to learn once if you're lucky.

Hey, thanks pal! You've been a really big help to me here and I appreciate it.

Here's to hoping I can get this all charged up using these organs. I bet it'll make those no good harpies think twice about attacking my caravan again. I sure hope this works.

Either way you've done your side of the deal. Take this for your trouble.
Research Access
Your actions show you are one who respects knowledge. The library is open for use in your studies.
Unending Torment
Deliver the Abominable Head to Master Apothecary Faranell within the Undercity.

<As the creature falls, its head comes toppling off. It seems as if it has been reattached several times, and the connection gets weaker with each reconnection.

Someone in the Undercity would know more about this unique abomination.>
What have we here?

Oho! I believe I know this head. A cruel joke by our Dark Lady. A delicious one at that.

I think I have a use for this.
Unending Torment
Bring the Head of the Baron to the body of Othmar in the Undercity.

We craft abomination heads all the time, but this one is special. It belonged to a Grand Marshal of the Alliance once. A particularly unpleasant one. Othmar, I believe its name was. The Dark Lady had the pleasure of dispatching this one herself.

Ooh the secrets it could tell if it could talk. And it can! If we reattach it to an appropriate host.

Go ahead and place it next to the available body in the next room. But don't attach it. Not yet.
<The abomination remains lifeless without a head to control it.>

<The body twitches to life, panicking as it relives its final moments.>

You...
Unending Torment
Report your findings to Master Apothecary Faranell in Undercity.

You... abomination...

Why should... help you...

Be gone...
Not cooperating, eh? Excellent. I always love a challenge.
Unending Torment

Collect a Toxic Skullcap from Tawny Grisette in the Trade Quarter, Blisterweed near the Herbalism Trainer, and Essence of Agony from the poison vendor in the Rogues' Quarter for Master Apothecary Faranell in Undercity.

With the head reattached, all we need now is to bind it to the Dark Lady's will. This should not be a problem. The beast barely has brains left as it is after all the beatings it's taken.

We simply need to motivate it.

Fetch me a Toxic Skullcap from Miss Grisette in the Trade Quarter. Oh, and some Blisterweed from our local herbalist trainers, the Alliestars. Feel free to just take some, they owe me. And lastly a bit of Essence of Agony. Any old poison vendor should do.

We have a potion to make!
It will be ever so lovely to have our lost sheep returned to the fold, don't you think?
These will do nicely. We will see how much bravado our honored guest retains after he is subjected to my masterpiece.
Unending Torment
Inject the Hissing Serum into the system above Othmar's body for Master Apothecary Faranell.

I have concocted a lovely serum that our new guest is sure to find quite... stimulating.

Take this. Feed it into the workings dripping from above him. Let's see if we can't show him why it's in his best interest to serve loyally.

And try not to drop it. I can't afford a new assistant.

For Othmar's crimes against the Dark Lady, placing him under that oozing specimen is the least he deserves.

And it's funny...

Excellent. We'll let his flesh simmer for awhile. Give him time to acclimate to his new home.

I have no further use for the wretch for now, but we shall keep an eye on him. I have many plans for Othmar's future.
Rocks to Rests
Return $1oa Smooth Boulders to Thra behind Grommash Hold.

Hey! You've got time to help us out! I know you do, I can tell by the way you smiled watching the game we're playing.

This spot behind Grommash Hold is nice because it's clear enough for us to set up our figures. But what stinks is we don't have enough rocks for chairs or tables.

You're big and strong... d'ya think you could carry back some medium-sized rocks, smooth enough to sit on if we need a rest?
It's nice to not have to always sit in the dirt!

How can you even hold all of those boulders!

Those are great. Most even have a nice flat side, too. Now that you carried them all the way over here we can scoot them around in the dirt, right where we want 'em.

Thanks, $N!
Traditions of the Bluff

Purchase a Bundle of Herbs from Nida the herbalist, a Bundle of Cedar Twigs from Nata the enchanting supplier, and Sinew Thread from Mahu the leatherworking supplier and Ceremonial Flint and Tinder from Naal the cooking supplier.

Combine the items and sprinkle the incense off of Hunter's Rise.

Blessings of An'she, friend.

We tauren have a tradition of scattering incense to the winds and I was hoping you'd be interested in honoring this tradition.

You will need to craft the incense by purchasing herbs from Nida, cedar from Nata, sinew thread from Mahu in the mid rise, and ceremonial flint and tinder from Naal on the upper rise. Once you have these items, combine them and spread them off the south facing cliff of Hunter's Rise.

You will find a mat and incense at the ceremonial site.

There are many occasions one may choose to spread incense to the winds. You could be asking the Earthmother to watch over someone, bless a hunt, celebrate an occasion, or even to seek guidance from our ancestors.

Or it could be something else entirely.

Though the act is done with reverence, it is not strictly a ceremonial affair. Typically there are certain traditional steps observed when performing this act, but many tribes have differing practices.

You have done well.

I thank you for taking the time to perform one of our time-honored traditions, $r. I hope that as you travel you will find plenty of occasions you wish to give thanks for.

Should you ever wish to perform the ritual again, you should be able to repurchase the components I sent you to collect.

Go with An'she's warmth.
Pigments for Paints
Tah Winterhoof in Thunder Bluff wants $1oa Mirkweed Pods from Mirkfallon Lake.

Greetings, friend. I wonder if I may ask a favor of you? I have just run out of red pigment for my paints, and I am looking for one with younger hooves to make the long journey into the Stonetalon Mountains on my behalf.

In the middle of the mountain pass there lies a large circular lake, Mirkfallon Lake, that has a unique plant that grows within its waters. The pods of this plant, mirkweed, turn a vibrant red when dried. Gather the pods of this plant for me, and I will reward you well for your efforts.
Silky Sutures
Return 12 Surgical Spidersilk to Doctor Gregory Victor in Hammerfall, Arathi Highlands.

This encampment is being left to rot. The siege damage stands, unrepaired, as if neglect were policy. I won't permit that same decay here. The infirmary answers to me, and I intend to keep it functional.

We are nearly out of supplies. I'm going to need more equipment--enough to keep the workers and guards on their feet.

Under pressure, we can make quite an effective field suture using twisted spider silk.

$C, bring me some from the spiders that stalk these highlands.
Hides for the Forsaken
Bring Shelene Rhobart $1oa Duskbat Wing Membranes, $2oa Darkhound Hides and $3oa Vile Fin Murloc Skin.

One part of undeath no one mentions is what happens when we are injured. How does the skin of an undead heal itself?

Well, it doesn't.

Ours is a cursed life, $n. We must take from the living to further our own existence.

When we sustain an injury, we must replace our skin which usually means animal hides. Since different hide thicknesses are better for different places on our bodies a variety is key!

Bring me wing membranes of a duskbat, hides from a darkhound and skin of a Vile Fin murloc.

Have you gathered the skin I inquired about? Our stocks are running low.

It may seem odd to ask for murloc skin but it works well for internal membranes, or surfaces like cheeks or mouths.

Similarly, the duskbat wing membranes are especially suited for more delicate areas, like faces or fingers. It prevents the skin from being too... thick.
Ah, excellent! Thank you for acquiring these. I can promise they will be put to good use.
WRIGGLE.
Purchase Nutritious Slime Sludge and return to your befriended excitable slime. If it seems tired, try dancing with it again to catch its attention.

<The little slime seems delighted and is attempting to mirror your motions as you dance. It begins to look weary though.

The little slime hovers over a bit of sludge and absorbs it, looking slightly rejuvenated.

It seems all of this dancing has tuckered it out. Perhaps someone in the Undercity canals sells more of this nutritious sludge?>
Prompt Potion Runner
Bring the Unstable Potion to Doctor Martin Felben in the Apothecarium within the time limit.

You! Quickly, I need you to bring this potion across the slime canal to Doctor Martin Felben in the Apothecarium!

It has a very limited shelf life, and no I can't go myself, my knees rattle and pop out if I attempt to run.

Just another lovely side effect of undeath, apparently.

But we're wasting time! Here, take this and go!

<Alessandro makes a shooing motion.>

Ah, marvelous! I had been waiting for Alessandro's potion to arrive. The last six he sent destabilized along the way, but you've made it just in time!

Here, take this for your effort. That is all for now, unless you have other business with me?

If not, remove yourself so I may continue my experiments unhindered.
Business in Auberdine

Check on Gorbold Steelhand in Auberdine in Darkshore.

Borgus mentioned a boat on the southern-most dock in Stormwind Harbor that can take you there.

Pleasure to make yer acquaintance! Name's Borgus, of the one and only Steelhand family. You can always count on a Steelhand fer a fair deal!

A few weeks back me brother Gorbold joined up with a merchant stall in Auberdine. Plenty of coin to be made supplyin' ships there, let me tell you! Lucky sod.

I haven't heard from him since--mind checking on him if yer heading that way?

There's a new ship in the harbor that will take ye straight there. Head to the southern-most dock; can't miss it!

Old Borgy sent you? Always looking out for me.

We could certainly use another set of hands around here. Business has all but stopped with the recent tragedy, and I think you could help set things right.
Camping 101: Alchemy
Speak with Whuut in Orgrimmar to learn to craft a camping item for your profession once you have shown proficiency in your skill.

So, you chose to cook up brews and potions as an Alchemist. I'm sure that'll come in handy in your travels.

I reckon I know someone that can teach you how to craft a Mana Well for your camp. Build one of these and all of the healers and spellcaster types will come running to get a refreshing taste.
Camping 101: Blacksmithing
Speak with Dwukk in Razor Hill to learn to craft a camping item for your profession once you have shown proficiency in your skill.

So, you've become a Blacksmith. That's a great choice if you want to make sure your blades never dull.

Nature's Call
Collect $1oa Gnarlpine Totems and bring them to Tarindrella.

The Gnarlpine furbolg would not turn on their ancient allies so readily. We must learn more of their plight.

Search their abandoned homes for totems. If any survived the chaos of their departure, their engravings may tell us more of what happened here.

You'll find their camps along the western edge of the glen, though the grell and grellkin may have scattered them beyond.
Don't worry about any larger totems you might find. I wouldn't know what to do with them if you found a way to get them!

Oh, it's even worse than I thought.

These engravings tell us that the Gnarlpine began having nightmares of being wiped out by some great shadow. Before long, that fear turned to rage--and the shadow to their former elven friends. To be aware of your own mind slipping away from you...

Our only hope is that this may help us better understand what is happening on Teldrassil. Thank you for your aid, $N.
